job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: Natural phenomena like lightning and earthquakes often seem mysterious, but they follow clear physical principles. Lightning is not a fire or burning gas; it is a massive electric discharge caused by the accumulation of charges in clouds. When clouds rub against each other, they transfer existing charges, meaning friction simply redistributes charges rather than creating new ones. Similarly, static electricity is not a separate force from the current in our wires; both are forms of the same electric energy. On the ground, the Earth’s surface is divided into massive, rigid tectonic plates that move slowly over a semi-solid layer of the mantle, not a liquid ocean of lava. These plates are distinct from continents, as a single plate can carry both land and ocean floor. When these plates grind against each other, they release energy as earthquakes. Scientists use instruments called seismographs to record these vibrations, but these tools cannot predict future earthquakes. Furthermore, the Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning a magnitude 7 earthquake is significantly more powerful than a magnitude 6, not just slightly stronger. Finally, a lightning conductor does not attract lightning to a building; instead, it provides a safe, direct path for the electrical discharge to reach the ground, protecting the structure from damage.

items.evidence: When clouds rub against each other, they transfer existing charges, meaning friction simply redistributes charges rather than creating new ones.
items.q: Two clouds rub together and become charged. Where did their charge come from?
options: It was already there and only moved
It was newly made by the rubbing
It came from gas burning inside the cloud
It flowed up from electric wires below
items.explain: Friction only moves charges that already exist between the clouds; it does not create new ones.

wrong.why: mixes up the clouds' charge with current in wires

items.evidence: These plates are distinct from continents, as a single plate can carry both land and ocean floor.
items.q: Why is it wrong to say a tectonic plate is just another name for a landmass?
options: One plate can hold land and seabed together
Each plate is simply one whole continent
Plates lie under oceans but never under land
Plates float freely on a liquid lava ocean
items.explain: A single plate can carry both land and ocean floor, so plates and continents are different.

wrong.why: thinks plates are the same as continents
over-generalises from the ocean floor detail
thinks plates float on liquid lava

items.evidence: Scientists use instruments called seismographs to record these vibrations, but these tools cannot predict future earthquakes.
items.q: A town sets up a seismograph. What can it actually do for the people?
options: Record the shaking when a quake happens
Tell them the exact day of the next quake
Stop the plates from grinding against each other
Measure the charge building up in the clouds
items.explain: Seismographs record earthquake vibrations, but they cannot predict when future earthquakes will happen.

wrong.why: confuses measuring a quake with preventing it
mixes up the earthquake and lightning parts of the passage

items.evidence: Furthermore, the Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning a magnitude 7 earthquake is significantly more powerful than a magnitude 6, not just slightly stronger.
items.q: Earthquake A measures 6 and earthquake B measures 7 on the Richter scale. How do they compare?
options: B is much more powerful than A
B is only a little stronger than A
A and B are about equally strong
A is stronger because lower numbers are worse
items.explain: The Richter scale is logarithmic, so magnitude 7 is significantly more powerful than magnitude 6.

wrong.why: thinks one step means only slightly stronger
thinks numbers close together mean similar strength

items.evidence: Finally, a lightning conductor does not attract lightning to a building; instead, it provides a safe, direct path for the electrical discharge to reach the ground, protecting the structure from damage.
items.q: How does a lightning conductor protect a tall building?
options: It lets the discharge flow safely into the ground
It pulls lightning in to keep it from other places
It puts out the fire that lightning starts
It makes new charges that cancel the cloud's
items.explain: The conductor gives the discharge a safe, direct path to the ground; it does not attract lightning.

wrong.why: thinks charges can be newly created
